crime_highlights: Mr. B. would show E.D. explicit pornographic material on his cellphone, both videos and pictures, of sexual acts between adults and between adults and children.
the sexual incidents escalated in frequency between 2017 and 2022 and became an almost daily occurrence
Mr. B. told E.D. not to tell her mother, […], friends or teachers about the sexual touching.
she felt afraid during these incidents
rationale_highlights: the reduced moral culpability of Mr. B. as an […] man who has suffered because of the intergenerational impact of colonization
I concur with the Defence that this is the main issue.
sentences must be proportionate to the gravity of the offence and the degree of moral responsibility of the offender
I find a fit and proper sentence to be 40 months incarceration
this sentence best reflects his moral culpability in these circumstances
note: Court concurs on proportionality and cites background, but never says plainly it reduced culpability.

crime_highlights: Adam Drake discretely, but rapidly and forcefully, stabbed Pat Stay in the chest
the needless and senseless extinction of the life of a young and contributing member of the community
It was inflicted by an armed assailant on an unarmed victim.
rationale_highlights: The offender is Indigenous, which is statutorily recognized as a mitigating factor pursuant to s. 718.2(e).
Justices determining parole ineligibility are required to consider the unique circumstances of Aboriginal offenders even when sentencing someone for the gravest of offences.
judges must craft sentences that are meaningful to Aboriginal people by emphasizing the use of restorative justice and restraint
I have considered the appropriate mitigation related to the Gladue factors as described by Justice Hunt in Sylliboy.
note: Court only says it considered Gladue mitigation; para 36 says needle does not move.
